title: A family-facing growth chart
line: patient-facing SMART on FHIR demo, Epic sandbox
question: What would it look like for a family to see and understand their child's growth record between visits?
calls: flags computed from a z-score threshold at render time, not hand-written trend annotations per scenario. scripted copy cannot survive real record data.
read-only, no backend. this demonstrates the family-facing view; it is not a clinical product.
home-entered measurements stay in the family's own browser storage. there is no backend, and the data never has to leave the device.
falls back to a mock scenario when the SMART launch fails, so the app opens from a plain link without a launch context.
broke: the Turner teaching case had been narrated as a percentile drop the z-score rule would never flag. the mock percentiles had to move to values the computed rule actually catches.
Pages deployment needed explicit job permissions and newer action versions before it worked.
Epic's exact redirect matching makes a project-subpath URL a trap: site root and index.html are not the same registered value.
tried: scripted per-scenario trend insights went away once flags were computed from the threshold, since a hand-written percentile-drop story cannot follow real record data.
not_shown: percentiles are not from a validated engine, the midparental formula has no documented source yet, and it has never been run against a real Epic client
